transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It’s really nice to meet you. Um, is it okay if I sit here? Thank you. 

Well... I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling a little overwhelmed lately. I hope I'm explaining this right, I don't want to sound difficult or anything. But for about a year now, I’ve been... well, I’ve been trying to prove something, and it’s just really wearing me down. 

I’m a phlebotomist, so I see this stuff all the time, and I noticed that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. I know exactly how that sounds, and I promise I'm not trying to cause trouble. Everyone—like, all the doctors and my family—they keep telling me his numbers are fine. But... I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I just want to make sure he's getting the right care, you know? Does that make sense?
Have you had any other experiences like this—such as hearing or seeing things that other people don’t?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I'm... you know, losing touch with reality or anything. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I'm totally normal that way, I promise. 

It's just the lab results. I just... I look at the screen, and I know what I saw before, and then later it's different. That's all it is. Just the charts. Is it okay that I'm so focused on the charts? I just want to be a good daughter, you know? I hope you don't think I'm crazy for checking them so much.
Aside from the lab results, do you have any other beliefs that other people tell you are false?

Um, no. No, definitely not. It’s really just... just this one situation with my dad’s bloodwork. I’m actually a very logical person, usually. I go to work every day, I get along with my coworkers... I don't go around thinking, um, wild things or anything like that. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as difficult or... or paranoid? Because I'm really not, I promise. I just know what I saw on those specific charts, and it's hard to let it go when it's your own father. But other than that, no, my family and I agree on everything else in life. I don't have any other disagreements like this with anyone. 

I'm answering your questions okay, right? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful.
If someone showed you clear evidence that the lab results had not been altered, would you be able to accept that?

Um... I really, really want to say yes. I know that's what I'm supposed to say, and I promise I'm not trying to be stubborn. I would look at whatever evidence you showed me, of course I would. I always try to be open-minded. 

But... well, I’ve been trying to prove this for a whole year now. And no matter how many doctors or family members sit me down and tell me the numbers are fine, or show me the current printouts... I just... I know the chart doesn’t match what I originally saw. I know someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his results. I just can't unsee what I saw with my own eyes, you know? 

It’s really wearing me down, honestly. I'm so tired of feeling like I'm the only one who cares enough to fix this. I hope you can understand where I'm coming from? I really don't want you to think I'm just being difficult on purpose. I'm just trying to be a good daughter.
Have you ever believed that people were trying to harm, monitor, or interfere with you in other ways besides your father’s lab results?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I really hope I haven't made you think I'm completely paranoid, because I promise I'm not. I don't think anyone is following me or, um, trying to hurt me or anything scary like that. 

It really is strictly just this one issue with the clinic system and my dad's chart. Everything else in my life is completely normal. I go to work every day—I actually do blood draws myself, I'm a phlebotomist—and I never feel like anyone is out to get me there or interfere with my life. I get along fine with everyone, and nobody is monitoring me. 

I just want to be really clear that I'm not, you know, seeing conspiracies everywhere. I hope that makes sense? I'm doing okay answering these, right? I really just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you don't think poorly of me.
Has this concern ever spilled over into other areas of your life, or is it only about your dad’s lab results?

Um, no, it really hasn't. It's... it's strictly just the dispute about my dad's records. Outside of that, everything is completely normal. 

I still keep all my regular phlebotomy shifts, and I'm a really good employee, I promise. I pay all my bills on time, I take care of myself... um, I just manage all my normal day-to-day responsibilities like anyone else would. I really try hard not to let this one stressful thing affect the rest of my life, you know? I know how important it is to be reliable and keep things together, so I make sure I do. 

Does that answer your question okay? I just really want you to see that I'm functioning perfectly fine in every other way. I'm doing a good job explaining this, aren't I?
Have you ever had hallucinations, like hearing voices when no one is there?

Oh, goodness, no. Never. I promise I've never experienced anything like that. 

I know sometimes when people get stressed out, they might, um, imagine things or hear things, but that's definitely not me. My mind is completely clear. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I'm very grounded in reality, I really am. 

I just want to be absolutely sure you know I'm not... well, I'm not crazy or anything. I'm just a normal person dealing with a really frustrating situation with my dad's clinic. I hope you believe me? I'm trying to be as honest as I can so you can see I'm perfectly sane. I'm doing okay, right?
If I showed you proof that no one had changed your father’s lab results, would you still believe the results had been altered?

Oh, um... I really don't want to sound stubborn or difficult. I promise I'm usually a very reasonable person. It's just... well, for the past year, I've been trying so hard to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. 

I know people have tried to show me things, but... no matter how many doctors or even my own family members tell me the numbers are fine, I just... I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. It really doesn't. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds bad, and I don't want you to think I'm just ignoring evidence, but it's just been wearing me down so much. I really hope you don't think I'm being totally unreasonable. I'm just trying to be a good daughter and protect my dad, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to.
How old were you when you first became concerned that your father’s lab results were being altered?

Um, let's see... I'm 33 now, so I guess I would have been 32. It's really only been going on for about a year. 

It all started when my dad's medical problems got worse and he started needing frequent labs and appointments. Because I draw blood for a living, I just naturally started paying closer attention to his charts to help him out, you know? I promise I haven't been, like, obsessing over things like this my whole life or anything. It's just this one specific situation over the last year because I care about him so much and want to make sure his care is handled right. 

I hope that's the kind of timeline you were looking for? Am I giving you all the right information? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful.
What is the strongest evidence you have that your father’s lab results were altered?

Well, um... I guess I don't have, like, a physical piece of paper to show you right this second. I know that sounds a little flimsy, and I really hope you don't think I'm just making things up. I promise I'm not. 

It's just that I remember what I saw originally. I know what his numbers were supposed to be, and then when I looked again, they were different. And, well, I know my job, you know? I work with blood all day. I know how these things are supposed to look. But as for hard proof... I guess I don't have something I can just hand to you. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very good answer. I don't want to seem like I'm wasting your time or being difficult. I just... I know what I saw, even if I can't prove it right now. Is that okay? I hope I'm not frustrating you.
Has anyone else in your family or community ever shared this belief that your father’s lab results were being altered?

Um, well... no, not really. It's just me. I know my family... well, they just tell me the numbers are fine and that I should trust the doctors. And I really do want to, I promise! I'm not trying to turn my family against the clinic or cause any drama or anything like that. 

Since I'm the one who works in healthcare, I think they just don't look at the charts the way I do, so they haven't noticed anything being off. I know it probably looks a little bad that I'm the only one bringing this up. I really hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or making a big deal out of nothing. I'm just trying to look out for him since I know what to look for. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm giving you the answers you need.
Have you noticed any times when your thoughts feel jumbled or hard to follow, or when other people say it’s difficult to understand what you’re saying?

Oh... um, no, no I haven't noticed anything like that. I promise my thoughts are really clear. I mean, at my job, I have to be super focused all the time, making sure I'm drawing the right tubes and labeling everything perfectly. You can't really afford to be jumbled when you're doing that, you know? And nobody has ever told me I'm hard to understand... at least, I really hope they haven't. 

Am I making sense to you today? I'm trying really hard to explain things properly. I hope I don't sound confusing or anything... I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you exactly what you need to hear. Am I doing okay?
Have you ever felt like your father’s chart was part of a larger conspiracy or connected to other strange events in your life?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I promise I don't think it's some big crazy conspiracy or anything like that. It's really just this one specific thing with his clinic and his numbers. 

I really hope you don't think I'm, you know, one of those people who thinks the whole world is out to get them or that I'm seeing things that aren't there. I'm completely normal otherwise, I swear. Just going to work and doing my job. There haven't been any other strange things happening in my life at all. I'm just worried about my dad's health, that's the only reason I'm even bringing the chart up. 

I hope it's okay that it's just this one thing... I really don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or being paranoid. I'm just trying to be a good daughter. Am I explaining that alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you ever heard a voice talking to you when no one else was around?

Oh, no. No, I've never heard anything like that. I promise. I know some people hear things, and I feel really bad for them, but that's definitely not me. It's always just quiet when I'm alone, or, you know, just the TV or the fridge humming. 

I really don't want you to think I'm hearing voices or anything scary like that. I'm completely fine in that way, I swear. My mind is totally my own. I hope you believe me... I'm really trying to be as honest as I can so you have exactly what you need. Did I answer that the right way? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression about how I'm doing.
If you had to rate it from 0 to 100, how certain are you that your father’s lab results were altered?

Oh... um. Well, if I'm being completely honest—and I really want to give you the exact right answer—I guess I would have to say 100. Please don't think I'm just being stubborn or difficult! I really don't want to be a bother to anyone. 

It's just... for the past year, I’ve been trying so hard to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing things, or maybe holding back parts of his lab results. And I know... I know no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, and I really do try to listen to them, I promise I do! I want to believe them so I don't cause any trouble. But I just know the chart doesn’t match what I saw with my own eyes. 

It’s... it's really wearing me down, honestly, carrying all of this. I'm sorry, I hope it's okay for me to say that. I just want to be as helpful as possible for you. Does that make sense, why I'd rate it that high? I hope I'm not frustrating you or saying the wrong thing.
Have you ever believed that this concern about your father’s lab results was connected to other people or events outside the clinic, even in a small way?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I really don't think it has anything to do with anyone outside the clinic. I promise I'm not... you know, trying to make it into this huge, sprawling thing. 

It's really just the clinic. Just that one place, and the people who work there handling his chart. I haven't noticed anyone else acting strange, or any other events that seem connected. I really try to keep to myself and just focus on my dad's care. I don't want you to think I'm looking for trouble everywhere I go. 

I just... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that okay? I hope I'm answering these questions the way you need me to. I just want to be helpful.
Have you ever believed that the same people at the clinic were also targeting or interfering with other patients, not just your father?

Oh, gosh, no. No, I haven't noticed anything like that with anyone else. I really haven't. I mean, I try to mind my own business when I'm there with him. I don't want to pry into other people's lives or make it seem like I'm... like I'm accusing the clinic of some massive conspiracy against everyone. 

I really don't want to be that kind of person, the one who thinks everyone is out to get everyone else. It's just my dad's chart. That's the only thing I'm worried about, I swear. I hope that's the right answer... I just don't want you to think I'm blowing things out of proportion or making things up about the clinic as a whole. I'm really trying to be reasonable about all this. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you believe the lab results were altered in a way that could realistically happen in the clinic, or does it seem more like something impossible or very strange?

Oh, um... well, it's definitely something that could realistically happen. I mean, I'm a phlebotomist, so I know how the systems work, you know? It's not... it's nothing crazy or impossible like aliens or magic or anything like that. I would never think something like that! Please don't think I'm completely out of touch with reality.

It's just... someone logging into the electronic medical record and changing a value, or maybe mislabeling a tube before it goes into the analyzer. Just normal, everyday mistakes or... or intentional changes that someone with access could easily do. 

I really try to look at it logically, based on my own training. I don't want you to think I'm coming up with these wild, impossible scenarios. I just see how easily a few keystrokes can change a whole chart. Does that sound reasonable to you? I really hope I'm explaining it in a way that makes sense and doesn't sound too... too strange. I just want to be as clear as I can for you.
Have you had any trouble at work or in daily life because of this concern?

Well, um... I really try not to let it interfere with things. I pride myself on being professional at work, you know? But... I guess maybe there have been a few little hiccups. Nothing major! I just... 

Well, my family has sort of started leaving me out of some of the planning for my dad's appointments. I think they just don't want me to worry too much, you know? They know how much I care, so they're probably just trying to spare me the stress. And at work... well, I was hoping to move up into a lab supervision role, but lately, I feel like I'm not really being considered for it anymore. I guess some people might think I make issues with the records a bit too... confrontational? 

I really don't mean to be! I just want things to be accurate, especially when I know how important those numbers are. I try to bring it up nicely, I promise. Do you think it's bad that I care so much about the records? I just want to do a good job... I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult to work with.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people could not?

Oh, gosh, no. No, I've never experienced anything like that. I mean, hearing voices or seeing things... that sounds really frightening, but no, definitely not me. I'm completely, you know, clear-headed when it comes to that sort of thing. 

I just see what's right there in front of me, like the numbers on the screen or the labels on the tubes. Just the facts. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, that I'm hallucinating or losing my grip on reality. I'm just a very observant person, especially because of my job. I hope that's a good thing, being observant? I just want to reassure you that my mind is perfectly sound in that way. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
